column2: Cut raw meat and chicken on a separate board; then wash the board and your hands.
Dice the chicken small; chop the carrot and courgette smaller than the chicken.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the chicken for 6–7 minutes until white on all sides.
Add the vegetables and stir for 2 minutes; add the tomato.
Cook covered over low heat for 10 minutes; add 2 spoonfuls of water if needed.
Serve lukewarm with rice.
Mash the fish with the boiled potato using a fork; add the carrot and egg yolk and knead.
Make small patties, coat them in breadcrumbs and arrange on the tray.
Bake for 15 minutes, turning halfway.
Wash the spinach several times in plenty of water and chop finely; wash the rice.
Cook the mince for 5 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon, until it has completely changed colour.
Add the spinach, rice and water; cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes until the rice is soft.
Cut small circles from the flatbread using a glass.
Grate the tomato and drain off some of the juice; a wet topping makes the flatbread soggy.
Arrange the circles on the tray and spread with tomato; sprinkle with the cheese and corn.
Corn kernels are a choking risk; chop them finely or crush them lightly.
Bake for 8 minutes until the cheese melts.
Let cool and cut into slices the child can hold.
Melt the butter in a pan and cook the meat for 10 minutes until its juices are absorbed.
Add the chickpeas and water; cook covered over low heat for 30 minutes until the meat is tender.
Boil the noodles in unsalted boiling water for 10–12 minutes until very soft and drain.
Melt the butter in a pan and soften the carrot and peas for 4–5 minutes; you can add 2 spoonfuls of water.
Cut long noodles into 2–3 cm pieces.
Peel the courgette and potato and chop them small.
Bring the vegetables to the boil with the water; cook over low heat for 15 minutes until soft.
Add the butter and blend.
Cool for 5 minutes.
Temper the yoghurt with a few spoonfuls of soup and stir it in; don't boil again or it will curdle.
Preheat the oven to 190°C; grease a small ovenproof dish.
Peel the potatoes and slice 3–4 mm thick; thin slices cook evenly.
Arrange the slices overlapping in the dish and pour over the milk.
Cover with foil and bake for 20 minutes.
Remove the foil, sprinkle the cheese and bake 10 more minutes until golden on top.
A knife should slide easily into the potato.
Rest for 10 minutes and cut into small pieces.
Wash and pick over the green lentils; pre-boil for 15 minutes and drain.
Dissolve the tomato paste in the water in a pan; add the lentils and vegetables.
Cook covered over low heat for 20 minutes until the lentils and vegetables are soft.
Cut the chicken into small cubes the child can chew.
Mix with the yoghurt, olive oil and thyme and marinate in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Arrange the chicken spaced out on the tray and bake for 15 minutes, turning halfway.
Don't use skewers; they pose a stabbing and choking risk for children.
Let cool and break into small pieces.
Preheat the oven to 180°C; grease a mini muffin tin or use paper cases.
Whisk the eggs and yoghurt; add the flour and baking powder and mix just until combined.
Add the spinach and curd cheese and mix.
Bake for 18 minutes; a toothpick inserted in the middle should come out clean.
Leave in the tin for 5 minutes to cool slightly.
Trim the ends and strings of the beans and wash them.
Chop the onion very finely; peel and grate the tomato.
Add the beans and tomato and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the water; cook covered over low heat for 30 minutes until the beans are soft enough to crush with a finger.
Cut the beans into 1 cm pieces; long, stringy pieces are hard to chew.
Whisk the cold milk, cornflour and cocoa in a pan until lump-free.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 6–8 minutes until thickened.
Remove from the heat, add the mashed banana and stir until smooth.
Divide into bowls and cover with cling film touching the surface.
Cocoa contains theobromine, a caffeine-like substance; use a little and don't give it in the evening.
Peel the carrot and dice it small; chop the chicken small.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the chicken for 6–7 minutes until white.
Add the leek and carrot and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the water; cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Preheat the oven to 180°C; line a small ovenproof dish with baking paper.
Mash the ripe bananas smooth with a fork.
Add the oats, very finely chopped raisins and cinnamon and mix; leave for 5 minutes.
Press the mixture into the dish 1.5 cm thick.
Bake for 20 minutes until golden at the edges.
Cool completely in the dish, then cut into bars the child can hold.
Don't give raisins whole; they are sticky and a choking risk.
Roll the mince into soft chickpea-sized balls; then wash your hands.
Peel the carrot and potato and dice them small; wash the rice.
Bring the vegetables to the boil with the water and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the meatballs and rice; cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Cut a meatball in half: no pink should remain inside.
Halve the meatballs when serving; whole round meatballs can get stuck in the throat.
